ClaimElement.description:
One verifiable part of a claim.

Decomposition is what makes gaps specific. "The project slipped two weeks against the
approved baseline" contains a duration, a baseline and a comparison; checking support
per element is how the system can say *which* part is unsupported rather than shrugging
at the whole claim.
ClaimElement.title: ClaimElement

Confidence.description:
A computed confidence, inseparable from the inputs that produced it.

Constructed only via `Confidence.compute(...)`. The components travel with the value, so
any report, UI or evaluation can show *why* a number is what it is — and so a value that
looks wrong can be traced rather than argued about.
Confidence.title: Confidence

EvidenceGap.description:
A specific missing piece of support, and what would close it.

`missing` is written for a human to read: it appears in the UI and in the report's
Limitations section. A gap that says "more evidence needed" has failed at its job.

missing.description: The specific absent element, e.g. 'approved baseline completion date'
missing.title: Missing

EvidenceGap.title: EvidenceGap

EvidenceRef.description:
A pointer from a claim to a source location.

Produced when a claim is made. Resolution happens afterwards, in the binder (Phase 13) —
which is precisely why `resolution` defaults to `UNRESOLVED`: nothing counts as resolved
until something has checked it.
EvidenceRef.title: EvidenceRef

ExecutionSummary.description: What the run actually did. Every field is counted, never estimated.
ExecutionSummary.title: ExecutionSummary

Finding.description: A structured claim, with everything needed to judge whether to believe it.
Finding.title: Finding

FindingClassification.description: How much epistemic weight a claim is entitled to.
FindingClassification.title: FindingClassification

GapType.description: Why a claim element is unsupported. The type determines how to go and fix it.
GapType.title: GapType

Limitation.description:
Something that constrains how much the report can be trusted.

Generated from run facts — skipped tasks, unresolved gaps, degraded verification,
exhausted budget — not from the model's sense of modesty.
Limitation.title: Limitation

MissionDetail.description: A mission's current state, without the full event log.
MissionDetail.title: MissionDetail

MissionSummary.description: One row in the mission list.
MissionSummary.title: MissionSummary

ReportSection.description: One section. `narrative` is model-written; everything else is injected.
ReportSection.title: ReportSection

ResolutionStatus.description: Whether a citation was matched against content the system actually retrieved.
ResolutionStatus.title: ResolutionStatus

SectionKind.description: The report's fixed structure. Order here is presentation order.
SectionKind.title: SectionKind

SourceLocator.description:
Exactly where a piece of content came from.

This is what makes evidence checkable rather than decorative. "doc_A says the project
slipped" is an assertion; "project_report.pdf page 12, chars 400-520" is something a
reader can go and verify, and something the evidence binder can resolve against the
chunks actually retrieved.
SourceLocator.title: SourceLocator

Stage.description:
The phases a caller can show a progress indicator for.

Deliberately coarser than `EventType`: a user watching a run wants seven phases, not
thirty-nine event kinds. The event log remains the complete record.
Stage.title: Stage

TaskType.description:
The closed vocabulary of task types.

A plan referencing a type outside this set fails validation (Phase 7). This is the
second half of the intent-vocabulary defence: operations the agent claims to need must
map to task types it can actually execute.
TaskType.title: TaskType

VerificationIssue.description:
One specific problem found with a claim.

Issues are the verifier's actual output. A bare status tells the replanning loop nothing
it can act on; `element` plus `issue_type` tells it exactly what to go and fix.
VerificationIssue.title: VerificationIssue

info.description:
An adaptive, evidence-driven investigation engine.

Missions run in the background: `POST /api/v1/missions` returns a run id immediately and
`GET /api/v1/missions/{id}/stream` streams the run as it happens. Every finding carries the
source locators it rests on, and every claim the evidence does not support is reported as
unsupported rather than dropped.
info.title: JARVIS

post.description:
Store uploads and report what each one parsed as.

The response is the parse result, not an acknowledgement. A client that only learns a
file was accepted still does not know whether it will contribute anything to a run -
a 12-page scanned PDF with no text layer uploads perfectly and yields nothing.

schema.title: Response Upload Documents Api V1 Documents Post
Response List Missions Api V1 Missions Get

post.description: Start a mission. 202, not 201: the work is accepted, not finished.

Ask a mission to stop. 202: cancellation is cooperative, so it is requested, not done.

The run stops at its next await point - a tool call or model call boundary - and keeps
whatever it had already established.

get.description: The full event log, paginated. This is the run's reconstructable record.

schema.title: Response Get Gaps Api V1 Missions  Run Id  Gaps Get

get.description: The same report a human reads, as Markdown.
Server-sent events for a running mission. See ADR-008.
The task graph with live statuses, plus the waves that can run concurrently.
Whether the engine can actually run. Reports the model, not just a 200.
